content.text: I have inspected every responsive location. Only §§ 8.2 and 8.3 govern renewal; no other clause modifies the renewal term, notice window, or uplift.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: The renewal bargain sits at (indeed satisfies) the preferred position, so no redline is warranted. § 8.2 makes renewal automatic only on terms our playbook expressly permits: each renewal term is twelve months (not multi-year), Customer may opt out on thirty days' written notice (window ≤ 30 days), and Vendor must send a renewal reminder at least sixty days beforehand — with the additional Customer-favourable mechanic that a missed reminder extends the opt-out deadline to thirty days after receipt. § 8.3 caps renewal uplifts at the lesser of US CPI-U over the preceding twelve months and three percent, requires ninety days' notice of any increase, and bars increases on prepaid periods, meeting the preferred price-predictability element (and comfortably inside the 5% fallback). Nothing in §§ 8.1, 9 or 10, or elsewhere in the document, lengthens the notice window, extends the renewal term, or permits an uncapped uplift, so no walk-away trigger (>90-day window or automatic multi-year renewal) is present. § 8.1's fixed three-year initial term is not an automatic renewal, and the § 2.1 take-or-pay purchase commitment is a minimum-commitment issue handled under that rule; we do not re-flag it here.
